title: Collins Elite blocking UAP research as demonic
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Collins Elite blocking UAP research as demonic, about an unknown time at United States (no place named), and relays what a named person told them. As told, not a fact.

as_told.title: The Collins Elite study UFOs as demonic

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, has brought up several times a group he calls the Collins Elite, which he describes as a circle of evangelical Christians tied to the United States government. According to Michels, this group was one of the main things blocking research into UAPs, short for unidentified anomalous phenomena, the official modern term for UFOs. In one episode he links this to what Lue Elizondo has said. Elizondo is a former Pentagon official who ran a small office that studied unexplained aerial reports. In another episode Michels says the group looked at the phenomenon through a program called Stack Five at a place he calls Wright airfield, and decided it was all demonic. He credits this to an author, Nick Redfern, and his book Final Events. A researcher, Jason Simosa, adds that Redfern's sources say the effort was funded in 1952 through the CIA's Directorate of Plans, a branch of the US spy agency, with about twelve people working on it full time. Michels himself also calls the story a rumour at one point, and a guest named Maaneli Derakhshani says only that he has heard rumours of the group. If it were true, religious belief would have decided whether the government took the subject seriously.
